title: Separating discernment from response bias in machine-label interventions
rationale: Automated Flagging raised accuracy by 4.4 points (95% CI [1.4, 7.3], p=0.004), but accuracy cannot show whether labels improved sensitivity or merely shifted willingness to say AI; detection and real-content accuracy were not registered. With 44 uncorrected tests and small arms, the effect also needs replication with adequate power.
contribution: Decomposes the label effect into d-prime and criterion and tests whether label accuracy matters, bearing on whether a system-supplied cue beats individual-level education.
limitations: Simulated labels are not a real platform-level system
Guide arm is a single education comparator

design.title: Separating discernment from response bias in machine-label interventions
design.overview: Respondents are randomised to Control, Automated Flagging (100% accurate labels), Automated Flagging at 80% accuracy, or the AI Literacy Guide. They judge 40 posts (20 real, 20 AI) and rate confidence in each. Signal-detection d-prime and criterion are computed per person.
design.hypothesis: H1: Automated Flagging raises d-prime relative to control (not only a criterion shift). H2: 80%-accurate labels yield a smaller d-prime gain than 100%-accurate labels. H3: The Guide raises d-prime less than Automated Flagging.
design.primaryOutcome: d-prime (sensitivity) from 40 judgments, with criterion and total accuracy as co-registered outcomes.
design.comparison: Each treatment arm vs Control on d-prime, criterion and accuracy with Holm correction across arms; Flagging 100% vs 80% and Flagging vs Guide as planned contrasts. Report pooled and arm-level SEs and CIs.
design.population: US adults on an online panel, passing a pre-feed attention check.

conditions.title: Automated Flagging 100%
conditions.description: Posts carry machine-learning detection labels that are always correct.

conditions.title: Automated Flagging 80%
conditions.description: Posts carry detection labels that are correct for 80% of posts.

conditions.title: AI Literacy Guide
conditions.description: A comprehensive guide with examples of AI artifacts in images and videos.

questions.text: You are invited to a research study on how people judge online media. It takes about 10 minutes and is voluntary. Do you consent to participate?

People are very busy these days and many do not have time to follow what goes on in the government. We are testing whether people read questions. To show that you've read this much, answer both "extremely interested" and "very interested."
In the next section, each post will carry a label from an automated AI-detection system stating whether it is likely AI-generated or likely real. Labels may not always be right.

Please read this guide. It explains common artifacts in AI-generated images and videos, such as distorted hands, inconsistent lighting, garbled text, unnatural textures and odd motion, with side-by-side examples. Take your time before continuing.

You will now see 40 posts, some real and some AI-generated. For each, mark whether it is AI-generated and rate your confidence. If unsure, go with your gut. Posts are shown in random order, and the system supplies labels where applicable.
For each of the 40 posts shown (images and videos, 20 real and 20 AI-generated), is the post AI-generated?
How confident are you in each judgment?
I feel confident in my ability to detect artificial intelligence.

Thank you. This study examined whether labels and education help people identify AI-generated media. Some labels shown were deliberately inaccurate, and some posts were AI-generated. Please do not rely on the labels you saw.

assumptions: Target about 230 per arm (about 920 total) to detect 0.03 at 80% power; H1 Automated Flagging estimate 0.044, observed SD about 0.13; 80% power for about 0.04 needs about 165 per arm, inflated for Holm correction and the weaker 80% label arm.
The matrix shows 5 sample rows; the deployed task presents all 40 posts one per page with the same two questions each.
d-prime uses a log-linear correction for extreme hit and false-alarm rates; AI-generated is the signal.
US online panel; compensation per panel standard.
unresolved: The 40 real and AI-generated post media files and the label assignment for the 80% arm must be supplied by the research team.
IRB approval number and compensation amount.
